# self-update: rebuild the zsh completion dump after an update

**Motivation:** opening a Warp preset of two windows greets me with

```
compinit:527: no such file or directory: /Users/.../.oh-my-zsh/cache/completions/_kubectl0tTmH1
compinit:shift:529: shift count must be <= $#
```

A single new window is clean, so it looked like fallout from `self-update all` that heals itself. It is not: the trigger is *concurrent* shell startup, and an update merely makes it frequent.

**Diagnosis**

The `kubectl` ([#114](DOT-113.md)) and `docker` plugins of Oh My Zsh regenerate their completion file in the background on *every* shell start:

```zsh
() {
  local TMPPREFIX="$ZSH_CACHE_DIR/completions/_kubectl"
  zf_mv -f -- =( kubectl completion zsh 2> /dev/null ) "$TMPPREFIX"
} &|
```

`=( ... )` materialises a temporary file named `$TMPPREFIX` + random suffix — `_kubectl0tTmH1` — inside `$ZSH_CACHE_DIR/completions`, a directory Oh My Zsh puts on `fpath`. It lives for milliseconds.

When shells start at once, one shell's temporary file makes another shell count 1356 files against `#files: 1355` in the dump. On a mismatch `compinit` discards the dump and rescans `fpath` — and the file is renamed away mid-scan:

```zsh
for _i_file in $_i_dir/^([^_]*|*[\;\|\&]*|*~|*.zwc)(N); do
  IFS=$' \t' read -rA _i_line < $_i_file   # 527 — the file is already gone
  shift _i_line                             # 529 — the array stayed empty
```

So both messages come from the shell that *rescans*, not from one reading a corrupted dump — the dump itself stays clean. An update changes the mtimes of brew completions, Oh My Zsh and zsh itself (this one also moved zsh 5.9 -> 5.9.2), which forces exactly such a rescan in every window at once.

Two secondary findings: a shell that exits before its background job leaves the temporary file behind for good, permanently breaking the file count; and Docker Desktop appends its own bare `compinit` to `~/.zshrc` *after* the line sourcing this repository, so any guard has to survive past its own invocation.

**Decision:** drop the two plugins. `kubectl` and `docker` appear zero and twenty-four times in 15k lines of shell history, their aliases never; and brew already ships `_kubectl` and `_docker` in `site-functions`, which sits right behind the cache on `fpath`. The plugins were generating a duplicate of what was already there -- and that generation was the only thing putting temporary files into `fpath`. Without them the race cannot happen: there is nobody left to race.

This replaces the first attempt (`fix #877`, 2026-09-15), which rebuilt the dump from `self-update` and is reverted here. A `compinit -C` guard in `.zshrc` was also built and discarded: it did silence the race, but at the price of skipping `compaudit` and the discovery of newly installed completions on every start, and it treated the symptom while the cause stayed in place.

**Verified:** completions for `kubectl`, `docker` and `docker-compose` still resolve, from brew; the oh-my-zsh completion cache stays empty; 30 shells started in parallel from a cold state -- no dump, no cache -- print nothing.

**Out of scope**

- the same race for anyone who does use these plugins: 51 oh-my-zsh plugins write temporary files into `fpath` this way. Upstream keeps `TMPPREFIX` local to an anonymous function, so it cannot be redirected from `.zshrc`; a fix would need custom plugin wrappers with `ZSH_CACHE_DIR` pointing outside `fpath`;
- the second `compinit` that Docker Desktop appends to `~/.zshrc` -- harmless here, and that file is not part of this repository.

<!-- 2026-09-16T15:00Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/877#issuecomment-5699625478
Reopening: the fix in `fix #877` was aimed at the wrong target.

The diagnosis above blamed the dump — a temporary name landing in `~/.zcompdump` and every later shell reading it. That is wrong. Both messages are printed by the shell that **rescans** `fpath`, and the dump stays clean:

```zsh
for _i_file in $_i_dir/^([^_]*|*[\;\|\&]*|*~|*.zwc)(N); do
  IFS=$' \t' read -rA _i_line < $_i_file   # 527 — the file is already gone
  shift _i_line                             # 529 — the array stayed empty
```

The rescan is triggered by the file count: a parallel shell's `_kubectlXXXXXX` makes `compinit` see 1356 files against `#files: 1355` in the dump, discard it and scan. So the trigger is *concurrent shell startup*, not an update — `self-update` only makes rebuilds frequent. It reproduces with four simultaneous shells and no update involved.

`refresh_completions` therefore cut the noise but did not remove the race. The actual guard is a `_safe_compinit` wrapper that forces `compinit -C`, so the file-count check never runs and nothing rescans `fpath`. `refresh_completions` keeps its place as the one deliberate, audited rebuild of the dump.

Two things found along the way: a shell exiting before its background job leaves the temporary file behind permanently, breaking the count for good; and Docker Desktop appends its own bare `compinit` to `~/.zshrc` after the line sourcing this repository, so the guard has to re-arm itself.
